knowledge-base.overview: Language-specific idioms, guardrails, and patterns for PHP 8.1+. Loaded automatically when agents work on .php files or composer.json. Applies to web applications, APIs, CLIs, and microservices. Covers strict types, PSR standards, modern PHP features (enums, readonly, fibers), error handling, security, and testing.

core-principles.principle: Every PHP file starts with `declare(strict_types=1)`. Non-negotiable.
All parameters, return types, and properties must have type declarations.
Follow PSR-12 coding standard, PSR-4 autoloading, PSR-7 HTTP messages.
Prefer interfaces, traits, and dependency injection over deep class hierarchies.
Use PHP 8.1+ features: enums, readonly properties, fibers, named arguments, match expressions.

guardrail.rule: Every PHP file must begin with `declare(strict_types=1)` immediately after the opening `<?php` tag. Never omit it.
guardrail.bad:
<?php

namespace App\Domain;

class UserService { /* no strict_types */ }

guardrail.rule: Never use the `@` error suppression operator. Convert PHP errors to exceptions with `set_error_handler` at bootstrap instead.
Never use `eval()`, `exec()`, `system()`, `passthru()`, or the backtick operator with user-controlled input. Validate and escape all shell arguments.
All SQL queries must use prepared statements with bound parameters. Never concatenate user input into SQL strings.
Never catch bare `\Throwable` or `\Exception` without re-throwing. Catch specific exceptions and include context in messages.
All function parameters and return types must have explicit type declarations. Use union types (`string|int`) over `mixed`. Use `never` for functions that always throw or exit.
Use `password_hash()` with `PASSWORD_ARGON2ID` (minimum `PASSWORD_BCRYPT`). Never store plaintext passwords or use MD5/SHA1 for passwords.
Always escape output for context: `htmlspecialchars()` for HTML output, parameterized queries for SQL, `json_encode()` for JSON. Never trust user input.
All file operations must validate paths with `realpath()` and check the result against allowed directories to prevent path traversal.
Run PHPStan at level 8 (or Psalm) in CI. Static analysis failures must not be merged.
guardrail.bad: // phpstan.neon with level: 0 or no static analysis configured
guardrail.good: # phpstan.neon parameters: level: 8 paths: - src treatPhpDocTypesAsCertain: false checkMissingIterableValueType: true

guardrail.rule: Set secure session cookie flags. Always use `session.cookie_httponly`, `session.cookie_secure`, and `session.cookie_samesite`.
Use CSRF tokens for all state-changing HTTP requests (POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE). Validate on the server side before processing.
Prefer match expressions over switch. Match uses strict comparison, is expression-based, and has no fallthrough.
Never add a closing `?>` tag to pure-PHP files. Always use one `use` declaration per import, grouped and alphabetized.
Run `composer audit` before committing and in CI. Never run `composer update` in production — use `composer install --no-dev`.

project-structure.description: PSR-4 layered architecture for PHP applications.
project-structure.layout: myproject/ ├── src/ # Application source (PSR-4: App\) │ ├── Domain/ # Business logic, entities, value objects │ ├── Application/ # Use cases, command/query handlers │ ├── Infrastructure/ # Framework, database, external services │ └── Kernel.php ├── tests/ │ ├── Unit/ # Fast, isolated unit tests │ ├── Integration/ # Tests with real dependencies │ └── bootstrap.php ├── config/ # Configuration files ├── public/ # Web root (index.php entry point) ├── composer.json ├── composer.lock ├── phpunit.xml ├── phpstan.neon └── .php-cs-fixer.php

rules.rule: Domain layer has zero framework dependencies
One class per file; directory structure mirrors namespace
Keep `public/` as the web root with a single `index.php` front controller

pattern.name: Service class with constructor promotion
pattern.description: Strict types, PSR-12, readonly promoted properties, named arguments at call sites.
pattern.example:
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace App\Domain\User;

use App\Domain\Exception\ValidationException;
use App\Domain\ValueObject\Email;

final class UserService
{
    public function __construct(
        private readonly UserRepositoryInterface $repository,
        private readonly EventDispatcherInterface $dispatcher,
    ) {}

    public function register(string $name, string $email): User
    {
        $emailVO = Email::fromString($email);

        if ($this->repository->existsByEmail($emailVO)) {
            throw ValidationException::duplicateEmail($email);
        }

        $user = User::create(name: $name, email: $emailVO);
        $this->repository->save($user);
        $this->dispatcher->dispatch(new UserRegistered($user->id));

        return $user;
    }
}

pattern.name: Backed enum with behavior
pattern.context: Status fields, roles, permissions — any fixed set of values
pattern.description: PHP 8.1+ backed enums with methods for labels and permissions. Prefer over class constants.
pattern.example:
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

enum UserRole: string
{
    case Admin  = 'admin';
    case Editor = 'editor';
    case Viewer = 'viewer';

    public function label(): string
    {
        return match ($this) {
            self::Admin  => 'Administrator',
            self::Editor => 'Editor',
            self::Viewer => 'Viewer',
        };
    }

    /** @return list<Permission> */
    public function permissions(): array
    {
        return match ($this) {
            self::Admin  => Permission::cases(),
            self::Editor => [Permission::Read, Permission::Write],
            self::Viewer => [Permission::Read],
        };
    }
}

pattern.name: Readonly class as value object
pattern.description: All properties implicitly readonly. Immutable by construction. Ideal for Money, Email, UUID value objects.
pattern.example:
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

readonly class Money
{
    public function __construct(
        public int $amount,
        public string $currency,
    ) {}

    public function add(self $other): self
    {
        if ($this->currency !== $other->currency) {
            throw new \InvalidArgumentException('Cannot add different currencies');
        }

        return new self($this->amount + $other->amount, $this->currency);
    }
}

pattern.name: Domain exception hierarchy
pattern.context: All projects — define before writing service layer
pattern.description: Abstract base exception with error code. Named constructors on leaf exceptions provide context-rich messages.
pattern.example:
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace App\Domain\Exception;

abstract class DomainException extends \RuntimeException
{
    public function __construct(
        string $message,
        public readonly string $errorCode = 'UNKNOWN',
        int $code = 0,
        ?\Throwable $previous = null,
    ) {
        parent::__construct($message, $code, $previous);
    }
}

final class NotFoundException extends DomainException
{
    public static function forResource(string $resource, string $id): self
    {
        return new self(
            message: sprintf('%s with ID "%s" not found', $resource, $id),
            errorCode: 'NOT_FOUND',
        );
    }
}

rules.rule: Use data providers for parameterized tests
Mock external dependencies with Mockery or PHPUnit mocks
No database or network calls in unit tests
Each test method tests one behavior
All bug fixes include a regression test

testing.pattern:
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace Tests\Unit\Domain\ValueObject;

use App\Domain\Exception\ValidationException;
use App\Domain\ValueObject\Email;
use PHPUnit\Framework\Attributes\DataProvider;
use PHPUnit\Framework\Attributes\Test;
use PHPUnit\Framework\TestCase;

final class EmailTest extends TestCase
{
    #[Test]
    #[DataProvider('validEmailProvider')]
    public function it_accepts_valid_emails(string $input): void
    {
        $email = Email::fromString($input);
        self::assertSame(strtolower($input), $email->toString());
    }

    /** @return iterable<string, array{string}> */
    public static function validEmailProvider(): iterable
    {
        yield 'simple'        => ['user@example.com'];
        yield 'with subdomain'=> ['user@mail.example.com'];
        yield 'with plus'     => ['user+tag@example.com'];
        yield 'uppercase'     => ['User@Example.COM'];
    }

    #[Test]
    #[DataProvider('invalidEmailProvider')]
    public function it_rejects_invalid_emails(string $input): void
    {
        $this->expectException(ValidationException::class);
        Email::fromString($input);
    }

    /** @return iterable<string, array{string}> */
    public static function invalidEmailProvider(): iterable
    {
        yield 'empty string'  => [''];
        yield 'no at sign'    => ['userexample.com'];
        yield 'no domain'     => ['user@'];
        yield 'no local part' => ['@example.com'];
        yield 'spaces'        => ['user @example.com'];
    }
}

quick-reference.item: All parameters and return types required; use `string|int` over `mixed`
Prefer `match` over `switch` — strict, expression-based, no fallthrough
PHP 8.1+ backed enums with methods over class constants
PHP 8.2+ readonly classes for value objects and DTOs
Use named arguments for constructors with many parameters
Domain exception hierarchy; never bare `catch (\Throwable)`; chain with `previous`
Prepared statements always; never string-interpolated SQL
htmlspecialchars() for HTML; parameterized for SQL
realpath() + allowed-directory check for all file operations
@ operator is banned — convert errors to exceptions
PHPStan level 8 (or Psalm) — CI must pass
PSR-12 enforced via PHP-CS-Fixer or PHP_CodeSniffer
